sentence_stem: If I had studied harder last year,
correct_completion: I would be ready for the exam now.
full_sentence: If I had studied harder last year, I would be ready for the exam now.
acceptable_variants: I would be better prepared now.
I would have a better chance today.

options.text: I was ready for the exam yesterday.
options.why_wrong: This describes a past fact. A mixed conditional needs a hypothetical past condition with a present result, so the main clause needs 'would' plus a present meaning.

options.text: I have studied for the exam already.
options.why_wrong: This reports a real past action. It does not express the imagined result of a condition that did not happen.

options.text: I would be ready for the exam now.
I will be ready for the exam tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' is used for real future plans. In a mixed conditional, the main clause uses 'would' for an imagined present result.

grammar_focus: Mixed conditionals (past condition with present result)
explanation: The if-clause refers to an unreal past situation, so it uses the past perfect. The main clause refers to an unreal present result, so it uses 'would' with a base verb. Learners often mix up the tenses across the two clauses.
translation: Якби я минулого року займався більше, зараз я був би готовий до екзамену.
